blocks.text: Large part powder coating is what our Milton shop is built for: a 23 ft oven, a weight capacity of up to 6,000 lb and in-house blasting under one roof. Since 2012, Koojo Custom Powder Coating has finished more than 10,000 items, from single brackets to heavy fabrications and complete equipment frames.

This page sets out exactly what fits, how big work moves through the shop and how long it takes, so you can check your part before you send a drawing. Standard orders carry a 48 hour turnaround, and the shop is open Monday to Friday, 7 AM to 5 PM. Each limit is stated plainly, with no guesswork.

blocks.text: Few shops in the region publish a weight limit, so it helps to know ours before planning large-part powder coating. Size and weight both matter: a long, light frame may fit easily, while a compact but very heavy casting may need a closer look at loading and racking. Knowing both numbers early saves a wasted trip with large parts.
Will My Part Fit?

Your part will usually fit if it is shorter than 23 ft, inside the oven's width and height, under 6,000 lb, and has somewhere solid to hang or support it. Check those four points first, then send us the part dimensions for a final yes.

Measure the longest length, the widest point and the tallest point, including anything that sticks out. Add the weight if you know it, or the steel size and length so we can estimate it. Long parts such as beams, rails and structural steel members fit lengthwise, so length is rarely the issue for large parts; width, height and hanging points usually decide. If a part is close to a limit, photos of the welds and lifting points help us plan large part powder coating without surprises on delivery day.
Equipment and Process for Big Work

Big parts follow the same steps as small ones, but each step is planned around size and mass: blasting, pretreatment and masking, then electrostatic coating and a full cure in our large curing oven. Planning comes first, because large parts cannot be reworked cheaply.
Blasting

In-house blasting removes mill scale, rust and old coatings so the powder bonds to clean metal, and mobile sandblasting covers items that are too awkward to move. That step matters most in large part powder coating, where a missed patch is hard to fix later. Learn more about our [sandblasting services](/services/sandblasting).
Pretreatment and Masking

Chemical pretreatment improves adhesion and corrosion resistance, and masking protects threads, mounting faces and contact points. Our [powder coating surface preparation](/services/surface-preparation) page explains each step.
Coating and Curing

Electrostatic spraying wraps powder around big frames and into corners. The 23 ft oven then cures each piece at 180–200 °C, and heavy sections stay in until the metal itself reaches temperature, which is what keeps a consistent finish on powder coating for large parts.
What We Coat at This Size

Typical large parts include equipment frames, conveyor and automation structures, machine bases, structural steel, railings and gates, trailer and vehicle frames, and heavy machinery coating for plant upgrades. Small parts can ride along in the same order.

Our [industrial powder coating](/services/industrial-powder-coating) page covers the full service for heavy frames and machinery, and our [powder coating projects](/projects) page shows finished examples with specs and photos. Both are good places to see how parts of this size come out, and how the same quality carries from a single beam to a full skid of large parts bound for a new production line.
From One-Off Jobs to Recurring Volume

We handle one-off and repeat orders with the same care. A single oversized frame gets its own planned cycle, while batch coating suits repeat runs of matching parts, and recurring bulk work can be scheduled to suit your production calendar.

Customers with steady volume often book oven time ahead, which keeps large part powder coating on a predictable rhythm. For pricing and account options on volume work, see [commercial powder coating](/services/bulk-commercial-orders), which covers recurring orders in detail. Batch work also makes it easier to keep colour matched across large parts made months apart, and recorded colour codes make later reorders simple.
Quality on Every Big Part

Large parts get the same checks as small ones. We measure film thickness to ASTM D7091 across faces, edges and welds, test adhesion to ASTM D3359, and record the results, so a 20 ft frame meets the same standard as a bracket.
Readings are taken where big parts fail first: long welds, outside corners and the lowest edge of the hang.

Our quality system is certified by the Absolute Bureau of Certification, and test reports are available on request. The steps are set out on our [powder coating quality assurance](/certification) page, which applies to powder coating large parts as well as everyday work.
Timing and Lead Times

Standard orders are turned around in 48 hours from drop-off. Very large, heavy or complex items may need more time for blasting, masking and cure, so we confirm the timeline in writing when you request a quote.

Large Part Powder Coating FAQs

Short answer: if a part is within 23 ft and 6,000 lb, we can almost always coat it. These answers cover limits, measuring and mixed orders, and they are written for this page only, not copied from other pages.

blocks.q: What is the largest part you can coat?
blocks.a: Parts up to 23 ft long and 6,000 lb, within the oven's width and height. Send drawings for anything near a limit and we will confirm before you ship.

blocks.q: What if my part is heavier than 6,000 lb?
blocks.a: Call us before you ship. Some heavy assemblies can be coated as separate sections before final assembly, and we will tell you honestly whether that works for your part. Splitting a job this way can also make handling and delivery easier.

blocks.q: Can large parts and small parts share one order?
blocks.a: Yes. Small parts can be coated alongside large parts in the same colour, so one order covers a whole assembly with a matched finish and a single delivery.

blocks.text: Check Your Part Today

Send the part dimensions, weight, quantity and a few photos, and we will confirm fit, finish and timing for your large part powder coating job. Phone (905) 876-7060, or use the online [powder coating quote](/get-a-quote) form.
We are open Monday to Friday, 7 AM to 5 PM, and reply with clear next steps.
